Subject: Regional HA orchestration protocol: EU & APAC data-residency constraints

Team — looping everyone in for a short architecture review. SovereignBank has two separate residency constraints we need to satisfy for their production private deployment: EU-only customer data (primary) and APAC failover that can run inference but must not write logs or customer PII back to EU. The ask is to propose a hardened orchestration protocol that supports warm standby in APAC while ensuring data does not cross EU boundaries except for metadata required for control plane health checks (which must be sanitized).

Key constraints and questions:
- EU cluster must be the only location allowed to persist logs or KV cache containing request payloads. APAC nodes may cache model weights and KV for generation but must not persist request-level telemetry.
- Failover latency target: application-visible failover within 90s, with a soft degradation tier for throughput for up to 10 minutes while caches rebuild.
- Network policy: mutual TLS between site control planes, and a one-way data egress policy from APAC to EU limited to orchestration heartbeats (no PII).
- KMS/HSM: keys for data-at-rest must be EU-hosted; APAC nodes should be provided ephemeral keys for local disk encryption that cannot decrypt EU-backed archives.

Attached: network_diagram_v2.png, residency_matrix_v1.xlsx, runbook_snippets.txt

Please review the attached diagram and matrix; I want to lock the high-level protocol before we schedule a runbook dry-run with SovereignBank ops. Marcus (cc'd via Marissa) will own any open procurement work if we need dedicated cross-region bandwidth.

Immediate asks:
1) Marissa — can you validate the SLA implications of a warm-standby topology with the 90s RTO?
2) Vivek — confirm whether our current KV cache eviction and prefix-cache invalidation flow can support the no-persistence constraint in APAC.
3) Jonas — network/hardening notes; do we need a separate peering model or can we do per-customer routing policies on the same interconnect?
4) Anna / PacCloud — confirm if PacCloud can support one-way peering and provide an ops contact for the dry-run.

Thanks — I want to get a first-pass decision by EOD tomorrow so we can prep the runbook.

— Irene

Subject: Re: Regional HA orchestration protocol: EU & APAC data-residency constraints

Thanks, Irene — reviewed the matrix and diagram. High level notes: 
- SLA impact: Warm-standby as described will affect sustained throughput during failover. To meet 90s RTO we either pre-warm KV caches to 50% expected working set in APAC or accept a 2x latency penalty for the initial 90s while caches populate. The SLA addendum should call out transient throughput degradation for 5-10 minutes post-failover.
- Proposal: use a two-phase failover: (1) control-plane switch with traffic redirection (target <90s); (2) background cache rehydration with prioritized prefix loading (target <10 minutes).
- Billing/commits: if SovereignBank wants guaranteed sustained throughput after failover, we'll require reserved capacity in APAC (RD) — otherwise a temporary throttle is reasonable.

Implementation notes attached in runbook_snippets.txt. I recommend adding an explicit sanity-check step that validates no request payloads were written to APAC S3 buckets after cutover.

Next steps: I can draft the SLA clause and reserve capacity options if we agree on the two-phase approach.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions & Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi all — PacCloud ops here. Quick confirmations from our side: 
- One-way peering: we support a unidirectional overlay where APAC can reach EU control-plane endpoints for heartbeats, but we will enforce egress ACLs preventing APAC-to-EU payload transfers beyond the heartbeat endpoints. We can provide an ops runbook for the ACLs.
- Network topology: recommend separate BGP communities for the SovereignBank private interconnect so you can apply stricter route maps and avoid accidental leaking.
- Storage: we can provide region-local object stores that are not replicated to EU. For the ephemeral local caches we suggest ephemeral encryption (KMIP-based) with keys we rotate per node; integration with customer's KMS is possible for EU-only persistent artifacts.

We can do a dry-run next Thursday at 02:00 UTC — please confirm window and an ops contact to coordinate cutover scripts.

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary and decisions after internal huddle: 
- Approach: adopt Marissa's two-phase failover (control-plane switch, followed by prioritized cache rehydration). This meets the 90s RTO goal while being transparent about transient throughput loss.
- Data residency guardrails: APAC nodes will be started in read-only telemetry mode — they may collect in-memory telemetry for routing but are prohibited from persisting request payloads or logs to disk. Any attempt to write to persistent storage will trigger an automated tamper alert to the control plane and a rollback signal.
- KMS: EU keys will be primary for persisted artifacts; APAC will use ephemeral node keys that cannot decrypt EU archives. We'll document the key lifecycle in the runbook.
- Networking: ask PacCloud to provide the one-way peering ACLs and BGP community segregation; Jonas to own route-maps and network validation.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Marissa: draft SLA addendum and optional reserved-capacity pricing (due 2027-06-24).
- Vivek: produce a short tech note on cache eviction & prefix rehydration logic and a unit test plan (due 2027-06-24).
- Jonas: prepare a route-map validation checklist and ACL template for PacCloud (due 2027-06-23).
- PacCloud Ops: confirm dry-run window and provide ops contact (requested by EOD 2027-06-21; tentative dry-run 2027-06-24 02:00 UTC).
- Irene: schedule runbook dry-run and prep the customer pre-brief (Irene will schedule calendar invite).

Anna — can you confirm that the guardrails are sufficient from SovereignBank's compliance perspective, or point to any gaps we should address in the runbook?

I'll circulate the runbook draft after I get Marissa's SLA wording.
